pages.text: $(bold)Entering the Steel Age$()$(br2)Start with the existing Wrought Iron workshop: make Iron Machine Foundations, Frames, Casings, Plates and Fired Refractory Ceramics. Steel's first complete loop requires a Coke Oven, Blast Furnace and a refining furnace. Each is a distinct JSON multiblock. You cannot craft your first Steel from vanilla Iron and Coal.

$(bold)1 — Metallurgical Coke$()$(br2)Form the Coke Oven (3x4x3) using the next Visualize. Supply four ordinary Coal through its REAL Item Input and fuel at the controller. It outputs four Metallurgical Coke from its Item Output after 720 HEAT-supplied ticks. This fuel can then run the higher-temperature Blast and Refining furnaces. Coal carbonization vents volatiles; no fake Wood Tar or Coal Tar is generated.

$(bold)2 — Blast Reduction$()$(br2)Prepare Magnetite Concentrate in the existing ore workshop. Form the 5x5x5 Blast Furnace with REAL Item Input, Primary Output and Slag Output ports. Supply 4 Concentrate + 2 Metallurgical Coke + 1 Calcite through the input port's THREE recipe slots. Add Metallurgical Coke as firebox fuel at the controller, and connect a Bronze AIR Duct to the LEFT side-wall tuyere. The 1200-tick reduction produces 2 Pig Iron and 2 Slag. No AIR or no Coke means no finished iron.

$(bold)3 — Controlled Steel Refining$()$(br2)A Blast Furnace makes high-carbon Pig Iron; it is NOT finished Steel. Form the distinct 5x5x5 Refining Furnace with its input, primary output, slag output and left wall AIR tuyere. Insert 2 Pig Iron, fuel with Metallurgical Coke and supply sustained AIR from the existing blower. The 1000-tick refining process produces 2 Refined Steel Ingots and separate refining Slag. HEAT and AIR are consumed during powered progress.

$(bold)4 — First useful Steel$()$(br2)Use four Refined Steel Ingots and your existing Wrought Iron Forging Die to craft a hardened Steel Forge Die. Install it in the SAME Bronze Forge Hammer through the existing replaceable-part interaction. It lasts 1536 successful batches, versus 768 for Wrought Iron and 384 for Bronze. The upgraded die does not increase RPM, torque, output or bypass the timed hot-stock requirement.$(br2)Producing and installing your first Steel Forge Die completes the Iron-to-Steel gameplay handoff.

$(bold)5 — Steel II: Hot Stock$()$(br2)Steel cannot be rolled cold. Queue 4 Refined Steel Ingots in the existing Iron Forge Hearth; fire with a real solid fuel (Metallurgical Coke is supported) until the higher Steel HEAT threshold is reached. It returns the SAME 4 ingots tagged temporarily hot. Fuel is not the material input. Use the Steel Forge Die on the existing powered Forge Hammer to forge 1 hot ingot into 1 Steel Plate (20 RPM, 10 torque).

$(bold)6 — Steel Rolling$()$(br2)Craft Steel Roller Sleeves with 4 forged Steel Plates and existing Wrought Iron Roller Sleeves, then install them on your SAME Bronze Rolling Mill. With 16 RPM and 10 torque, roll 1 hot Steel Ingot into 1 Steel Bar. Reheat 4 Steel Bars in the Iron Forge Hearth and roll 1 hot Steel Bar into 4 Steel Rods. Steel stock quality is preserved, temporary hot NBT is removed from shaped output, and powered batches consume tooling life only on completion.

$(bold)7 — Steel III: Heavy Transmission$()$(br2)Steel Medium Gear (8 teeth) and Steel Gearbox (right-angle 1:1) can transmit 32 game-torque; Steel Large Gear (16 teeth) and Steel Shaft are rated 48. These figures are structural capacity, NOT new generated power. The same gear-ratio, direction, shaft, meshing and overload rules apply. Wooden and Wrought Iron bottlenecks still limit the network; the Water Wheel cannot magically deliver 32 torque.

$(bold)Steam-ready Drivetrain$()$(br2)Steel upgrades use the same Gear V2 connections as Wood/Iron. 16T Large + 16T Large mesh ONLY at perpendicular axes with one-block offsets along both axles, turning power 90 degrees. For parallel Large gears, bridge with an 8T Medium gear diagonally; the Large gears do not mesh directly. Medium + Medium connect adjacent (1:1); Medium + Large connect diagonally (2:1). Wrongly closed loops or incompatible sources stall, never create free mechanical power. Final gear visuals remain under MGC2 Studio.

$(bold)8 — Steel IV-A: Heavy Plate$()$(br2)No new multiblock is necessary. First roll Steel Ingots into Bars using the existing Rolling Mill with Steel Roller Sleeves. Reheat 4 Steel Bars together in the fueled Iron Forge Hearth (higher Steel HEAT threshold) and move the same 4 hot Bars to the existing powered Forge Hammer fitted with a Steel Forge Die. At 20 RPM and 12 torque, 320 powered ticks forge all 4 Bars into ONE Heavy Steel Plate. The plate contains four ingot-equivalents: a material-conserving forge-welded billet, not four free plates. Cold bars will not work and completed batches wear the die.

$(bold)9 — Curving a Boiler Shell$()$(br2)Craft one Steel Press Die by reinforcing the earlier Bronze Press Die with four normal Refined Steel Plates. Install that part in the existing Bronze Mechanical Press. Feed one Heavy Steel Plate through its REAL input port. With 18 RPM and 14 torque, the 240-tick powered forming recipe produces ONE Boiler Shell Section, preserving the Steel plate's quality/provenance. A Bronze Press Die cannot form this component; Copper Panels remain craftable with either die.

$(bold)Steam Plant Construction$()$(br2)A Boiler Shell Section is a fabrication component, NOT a functioning boiler. It has no fluid, HEAT, PRESSURE or STEAM capability. Later Steel IV work will define boiler end plates, flanges, valves and actual assembly consumers. Do not create or consume live pressurized steam until the Steam Age vertical slice. Current item models reuse existing Steel stock shapes as temporary MGC2 Studio placeholders.
